title: Fix long-queue starvation edge case in mixed-workload two-queue scheduler
author: Marcus Reed
release_notes: Fixes a starvation edge case in the mixed-workload two-queue scheduler where long requests could make no progress under sustained short traffic; adds regression coverage.
body:
Context
We hit an edge case during load tests (see #eng-runtime thread 1770417729) where long-context requests could starve indefinitely when the short queue remains continuously non-empty (e.g., 95/5 mix, short requests arriving at a rate that keeps short queue depth > 0).

Root cause
Our current aging/boost logic only applies when we consider a long request for dispatch. But in sustained short traffic, the dispatch loop effectively never reaches the long queue because the short queue always produces at least one eligible batch each iteration and the per-iteration class share enforcement is soft. In practice this becomes: "short wins every time" and long requests accrue wait time but never trigger a hard preemption.

Fix
- Change aging from a purely additive score to a thresholded "must-serve" promotion: if oldest long request wait_time_ms >= long_starvation_max_wait_ms, we treat LONG as temporarily high priority for at least one dispatch quantum.
- Make the promotion sticky for a bounded number of iterations (long_starvation_burst_iters) so we complete prefill and ensure decode makes progress, but cap it to avoid flipping the system into long-dominant behavior.
- Keep existing token budget guardrails intact: even in promoted mode we still respect per-iteration token budgets, but we allow LONG to consume the class share for that iteration.

Why this is safe
- The promotion only triggers after a long request has exceeded a configured wait threshold; default value tuned for canary to be conservative (2500ms).
- We cap the promoted burst to prevent "long takeover" under pathological long-only scenarios.
- The change is behind the existing mixed scheduler feature flag; no effect when the policy is disabled.

Config knobs
- scheduler.long_starvation_max_wait_ms (new, default: 2500)
- scheduler.long_starvation_burst_iters (new, default: 2)
- scheduler.long_aging_half_life_ms (existing, now used only for tie-breaking rather than progress guarantees)

Tests
- Adds a regression test that replays the starvation scenario: sustained short arrivals + one long request. Asserts:
  1) long request observes bounded time-in-queue (<= threshold + epsilon)
  2) long request receives at least one dispatch within N iterations
  3) short p95 does not blow up (test uses a small simulated scheduler + deterministic clocks rather than GPU runtime)

Bench notes
I ran the synthetic 80/20 and 95/5 mixes in the local simulation harness. This fixes the starvation case; the 80/20 baseline numbers are unchanged within noise. We should still validate on perf-canary once merged into the release branch.

Implementation details
- The dispatch loop now checks oldest_long_wait_ms each iteration (O(1) using tracked head timestamps).
- Promotion sets a local force_class=LONG for the next dispatch selection; it does not reorder queues.
- Metrics: increments scheduler_starvation_promotions_total{class="long"} and records scheduler_oldest_wait_ms{class="long"} to help verify in canary.

Changed areas
- runtime/scheduler/two_queue_dispatch.cc: promotion + sticky burst implementation
- runtime/scheduler/aging.cc: adjust aging semantics (tie-breaker only)
- runtime/scheduler/config.h: add new knobs + validation
- runtime/metrics/scheduler_metrics.cc: add starvation promotion counter
- runtime/tests/scheduler/mixed_workload_starvation_test.cc: new regression test
- docs/internal/runtime/scheduler_policy.md: update with starvation guarantee behavior

Checklist
- [x] Unit/regression tests added
- [x] Metrics added/updated
- [x] Config validation + safe bounds
- [x] Verified feature-flag behavior
- [x] Release branch cherry-pick ready

Review discussion highlights
Lena Fischer: "We need a hard progress guarantee; purely increasing score won’t help if we never look at LONG." -> Implemented thresholded must-serve promotion + sticky burst.
Sofia Ivanova: "Make sure this doesn’t create oscillation with token budgets; keep it bounded." -> Added long_starvation_burst_iters and kept token budget enforcement.
Sean Gallagher: "Add a metric we can alert on during canary." -> Added scheduler_starvation_promotions_total and oldest wait gauge.
Omar El-Sayed: "Ensure prefill/decode separation isn’t regressed." -> Promotion only affects class selection; prefill/decode hooks unchanged.

CI
- build-and-unit-tests: PASS
- runtime-scheduler-tests: PASS
- lint/clang-format: PASS

Merge
Merged via squash into release/runtime-1.18. Follow-up: once perf-canary picks up the new release artifact, we should confirm starvation_promotion counter remains near-zero in normal mixes and only spikes in the synthetic 95/5 scenario.
